title: Research OS Executor Return Contract
description: Formal, tool-agnostic return schema for any executor (Codex, WorkBuddy, script, human) acting on a Research OS dispatch spec. The executor returns only observations with explicit provenance. It may NOT self-approve, may NOT mark the episode complete, and may NOT raise any claim ceiling. The OS diagnoses the returned state; returning 'success' never changes episode status on its own.

observations.description: Raw observations the executor gathered. Each entry is a plain string or object; the OS decides what (if anything) it supports.

source_identities.description: Exact, resolvable identity of every source actually consulted (doi, url, file path, record id). Vague references are not acceptable.

access_level.description: What the executor actually accessed, not what it claims to have read.

calculation_result.description: Structured result of any numeric recomputation or derivation. Null if none was performed.

errors.description: Every blocker, exception, or denied access encountered.

provenance.description: Append-only provenance records: tool used, command, inputs, outputs, hashes where relevant.

timestamps.description: Exact clock times for access and return. Batch-identical accessed_at values are NOT proof of reading and are flagged by the OS.

self_approved.description: PROHIBITED. An executor must never assert self-approval. Presence of this key is rejected by the OS.

mark_episode_complete.description: PROHIBITED. An executor must never mark the episode complete. Presence of this key is rejected by the OS.

claim_ceiling.description: PROHIBITED. An executor must never raise or assert a claim ceiling. That is an OS/gate decision.
